description_ru: Alluvial deposits: gravel, sand and silt, 1-10 m; terraces and plains of former floodplains and deltas (Nelson and Hayes rivers)
Marine shoreline deposits (Tyrrell Sea): sand and gravel, 1-3 m; beaches and bars from till and glaciofluvial materials
Marine nearshore and intertidal deposits: silt, sand and clay, 1-3 m, upward-coarsening offlap; commonly over till
Glaciolacustrine basin deposits (glacial Lake Agassiz): clay and silt, 2-15 m; nearly unbroken blanket in low relief areas
Glaciolacustrine shoreline deposits: sand, gravel and rock rubble, up to 3 m; beach ridges, bars, spits
Glaciofluvial ice-contact deposits: sand and gravel, 15-90 m; kame moraines, interlobate moraines, kames, eskers
Glaciofluvial channel deposits: well sorted sand and gravel, 1-15 m; plains and terraces in valleys
Ground moraine: sandy and silty till, 1-8 m; nearly flat blanket, locally under a glaciolacustrine veneer
Till veneer: till and minor clay, silt, sand, gravel, up to 2 m, over rock with abundant outcrops
Hummocky moraine: till 5-30 m; ridges, knolls, hummocks; with glaciofluvial ice-contact deposits
LM / LR (same colour; told apart by labels only): glaciolacustrine discontinuous veneer, 1-2 m, largely over till with areas of till and rock (LM) or largely over rock with abundant outcrops (LR)

Rc / R (same colour; told apart by labels only): rock outcrop and rock thinly covered by drift; Rc dolomite, calcareous shale and limestone; R igneous and crystalline metamorphic rock (Precambrian Shield)
